profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CyrusOne campus sits in Chandler, Arizona. Wikipedia coverage of CyrusOne states the company acquired 55.9 acres in Chandler in September 2011 for data center construction, part of its early 2010s national expansion under Cincinnati Bell ownership. CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten and was taken private in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Global Infrastructure Partners acquired it for 15 billion dollars. No building specific address or individual MW figures were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
CyrusOne PHX5 publishes 169 MW of IT capacity across 2,000,000 square feet of technical space in Chandler, Arizona. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 169 MW supports roughly 4,225 racks; at 100 kW per rack, a figure increasingly associated with GPU-dense deployments, the same power supports roughly 1,690 racks. Those are assumptions about rack density, not operator claims. The site does not publish a stated rack count. 169 MW is a large number in absolute terms, and the physical footprint of two million square feet is consistent with a multi-building campus rather than a single hall.

Among the four facilities in Arizona for which this site has read a published megawatt figure, PHX5 ranks first, accounting for 169 of the 512.02 MW total, or roughly 33 percent of the published capacity this site has on record for the state. Arizona has 56 mapped facilities in total, and most of them publish no capacity figure, so the true state total is higher than 512 MW by an unknown amount. What the ranking does confirm is that PHX5 is the largest single site among those whose operators have published a number this site has read.

The certifications qualify the campus for specific regulated workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 qualify it for financial and operational audit requirements. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment-card data environments. HIPAA qualifies it for protected health information. ISO 27001 qualifies it for internationally audited information security management. FISMA qualifies it for certain U.S. federal government workloads. TIA-942 certifies the facility against a published data center design standard. Green Globes records a formal sustainability assessment. Who occupies the campus, and whether any AI training workloads are running there, is not published.
